what: highlight "Dutch bank ING purchased Barings Bank in 1995 for the nominal sum of £1"
said: In March nineteen ninety-five, one of the oldest banks in Britain was sold to a Dutch bank for exactly one pound. About a dollar and a half.

what: highlight "It was founded in 1762 by Francis Baring"
said: This was not some small shop. Barings had been in business since seventeen sixty-two. It was two hundred thirty-three years old.

what: highlight "the Louisiana Purchase , which doubled the size of the United States"
said: It had helped pay for the Louisiana Purchase, the giant land deal that doubled the size of the United States.

what: highlight "the sixth great European power"
said: It even helped finance the American government during the War of eighteen twelve. Around eighteen eighteen, people called it the sixth great power in Europe.

what: highlight "overexposure to Argentine and Uruguayan debt"
said: Barings had nearly died once before. In eighteen ninety, it lent too much to Argentina and Uruguay. When Argentina came close to defaulting, Barings did not have enough money to cover the losses.

what: highlight "The rescue avoided what could have been a worldwide financial collapse"
said: The Bank of England organized a group of banks to rescue it. That rescue avoided what could have been a worldwide financial collapse.

what: highlight "Losses eventually reached £827 million"
said: His losses reached eight hundred twenty-seven million pounds. That was about one point four billion dollars, twice the bank's available trading capital.

what: highlight "on a salary of £12,000"
said: He joined Barings on a salary of twelve thousand pounds a year.

what: highlight "In April 1992, Barings decided to open a Futures and Options office in Singapore"
said: He was only twenty-five. He had a new wife, a new country, and a trading floor full of shouting brokers in bright jackets. It was exciting, fast, and very loud.

what: highlight "Neither Leeson nor Barings disclosed this denial when he applied for his licence in Singapore."
said: There was a warning sign before he even left. Leeson had been denied a trading license in Britain, for not reporting a debt judgment against him. Neither he nor Barings mentioned this when he applied for his license in Singapore.

what: highlight "£10 million, which accounted for 10% of Barings' annual profit"
said: At first, Leeson looked brilliant. His trades made Barings about ten million pounds, around ten percent of the whole bank's yearly profit.

what: highlight "He earned a bonus of £130,000 on his salary of £50,000"
said: That year, he earned a bonus of one hundred thirty thousand pounds on top of a fifty thousand pound salary. In London, people started calling him a star.

what: highlight "by also making Leeson head of settlement operations for SIMEX"
said: At Barings Singapore, Leeson did both. He ran the trading, and he was also in charge of the settlement office that recorded and checked the trades.

what: highlight "With authority to settle his own trades, Leeson was able to operate with no supervision from London"
said: These jobs would normally be held by different employees. With the power to settle his own trades, Leeson could work with no real supervision from London.

what: highlight "Leeson used one of Barings' error accounts"
said: Then he used a special kind of account. Banks keep error accounts, to fix small mistakes, like a trade entered wrongly.

what: highlight "costing Barings £20,000"
said: The first mistake was small. Someone on his team was told to buy twenty futures contracts for a client, but sold them instead. It cost the bank twenty thousand pounds.

what: highlight "How account 88888 sank Britain's oldest bank"
said: Leeson's error account had a number that became famous. Eight eight eight eight eight. Eight is a lucky number in Chinese culture.

what: highlight "to prevent the London office from receiving the standard daily reports on trading, price and status"
said: He even changed the account so that London would not get the normal daily reports on it. The one place that would show the losses was switched off.

what: highlight "This amount then ballooned to £208 million by the end of 1994."
said: Two hundred eight million pounds was far more than Leeson could ever earn in a lifetime. But on paper, in London, he still looked like their best trader.

what: highlight "every time he lost money, he would bet double the amount that was lost to recoup the amount"
said: How do losses grow like that? Leeson followed what is called a doubling strategy. Every time he lost, he bet double, hoping one win would erase everything.

what: highlight "after which he vowed not to use the account again"
said: The scary part is that it worked once. In nineteen ninety-three, he managed to wipe out a six million pound hole, and promised himself he would never use the account again.

what: highlight "He falsified trading records in the bank's computer systems"
said: To keep the game going, he needed cash. So he used money that belonged to other parts of the bank, and changed records in the bank's computer systems.

what: highlight "betting that the Japanese stock market would not move significantly overnight"
said: On January sixteenth, nineteen ninety-five, Leeson made a big bet. He bet that Japan's stock market would stay calm, and not move much overnight.

what: highlight "At least 5,000 people died, around 4,600 of them from Kobe."
said: At least five thousand people died. Nearly four hundred thousand buildings were badly damaged.

what: highlight "120 of the 150 quays in the port of Kobe"
said: The earthquake damaged nearly four hundred thousand buildings and wrecked one hundred twenty of the one hundred fifty docks in Kobe's port, one of the busiest in the world.

what: highlight "images of the collapsed elevated Kobe Route of the Hanshin Expressway appeared on front pages of newspapers worldwide"
said: Pictures of a collapsed elevated highway in Kobe appeared on the front pages of newspapers around the world.

what: highlight "the Kobe earthquake upset the Asian financial markets"
said: It was a human tragedy first. And it also shook Japan's stock market badly, which hit Leeson's positions hard.

what: highlight "betting that the Nikkei Stock Average would make a rapid recovery"
said: Instead of stopping, Leeson did what he always did. He doubled down. He bet that the Nikkei would bounce back quickly.

what: highlight "and fled Singapore on 23 February."
said: On February twenty-third, nineteen ninety-five, Nick Leeson left a note on his desk. It said, I'm sorry. Then he fled Singapore.

what: highlight "The Bank of England attempted an unsuccessful weekend bailout"
said: The Bank of England tried to arrange a rescue over the weekend. It failed.

what: highlight "Barings was declared insolvent on 26 February 1995"
said: On February twenty-sixth, Barings was declared insolvent. Insolvent means a company cannot pay what it owes. Employees around the world did not get their bonuses.

what: highlight "The collapse cost another £100 million."
said: Cleaning up the collapse cost another one hundred million pounds on top of the trading losses.

what: highlight "Barings Bank no longer has a separate corporate existence"
said: Over the next ten years, ING sold off the pieces. By two thousand five, Barings no longer existed as its own company, only as a name on a few businesses.

what: highlight "Leeson was arrested in Frankfurt"
said: Leeson ran through Malaysia and Thailand, and was finally arrested in Frankfurt, Germany. He was sent back to Singapore to face trial.

what: highlight "after serving at least two-thirds of his sentence (four years and four months)"
said: He served about four years and four months before he was released, partly because he was seriously ill with colon cancer.

what: highlight "sentenced him to six and a half years in Changi Prison"
said: He served about four years and four months before he was released, partly because he was seriously ill with colon cancer.

what: highlight "the book was made into a film of the same name starring Ewan McGregor"
said: In prison, he was diagnosed with cancer. He survived. Later, he wrote a book called Rogue Trader, which became a movie starring Ewan McGregor.

what: highlight "several observers placed much of the blame on the bank's own deficient internal control and risk management practices"
said: After the collapse, many experts said the biggest failure was not Leeson alone. It was the bank's weak internal controls and risk management.

what: highlight "A number of people had raised concerns over Leeson's activities but were ignored."
said: Some people had raised concerns about Leeson's trading. They were ignored.

what: highlight "it ought to be read by banking managers and auditors everywhere"
said: One review of Leeson's book in the New York Times said it should be read by banking managers and auditors everywhere.

what: highlight "losses attributed are estimated at € 4.9 billion"
said: When the bank unwound those positions in January two thousand eight, during a market drop, it estimated the losses at four point nine billion euros.

what: highlight "Kerviel generated €1.4 billion in hidden profits by the end of 2007"
said: Just like Leeson, the trader had looked very successful at first. According to the BBC, he had built up one point four billion euros in hidden profits by the end of two thousand seven.

what: highlight "Société Générale's own wrongs were later established by a French jurisdiction"
said: Courts later found that the bank had its own failures too, and cancelled the four point nine billion euro penalty against the trader himself.
